utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody. May we hear the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. This is Case Number IT-97-24, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And the limited appearances for the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Good morning Your Honours. Nicholas Koumjian, soon to be joined by Ruth Karper for the Office of the Prosecutor and I could briefly explain as the Defence introduce themselves. What she is doing now, she is getting some new documents I would like to briefly discuss with the court

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Branko Lukic and John Ostojic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Two issues before we start. I have to inform the parties that the Bench decided to summon, under Rule 98 sentence 2, Mr. Dusan Baltic for Wednesday, the 18th of September, 9.30. So the input would be helpful, but in case there should be any kind of hindrance for this witness, it should be left for an in-house witness. But in principle, it should be the entire day available for this additional witness. Second, I think yesterday's hearing was not one of the highlights of that what we have heard in the past in this case. I think the expertise was not indeed, to be very diplomatic, helpful for the purposes of our case, especially because not based on that what we have heard until now in courtroom. To a certain extent, we had the impression to be misled by the examination-in-chief having had the impression that indeed the cross-check was done on the basis of viva voce testimony and admitted 92 bis evidence. Therefore, I have to re-emphasise that we expect that we get an additional table based on the names listed in the annex of the fourth amended indictment, indicating in three columns whether this person was listed as missing person in the updated list of missing persons, second column whether this person was declared dead by court in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and third column, whether or not this person was exhumed and then to add in this column where the place of exhumation was. In addition, we need, no doubt, the law applicable for the decision of the courts of Bosnia-Herzegovina to declare a person dead. I think this will be helpful in addition, but to turn to the other side, I would really ask the Defence not to overstate. Yesterday the cross-examination has been extremely helpful, but on the other hand, some overstatements are watering down to a certain extent these results and please beware when looking to the Bench you find three professional Judges. There is no jury. And please don't blame an expert witness for that what was done responsible for the results of those persons having made the request and not the person having worked on this issue. Therefore, I hope that we come back to the climate as we were acquainted with in the past already now and already today when we hear now today's witness, Mr. ten Camp. But I had the impression that the Office of the Prosecutor wants to make some remarks before we start.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. Before I address the issue related to document signatures, can I briefly just address the Court's comments regarding the witness yesterday. Mr. Sebire, as he made clear, did not come here as an expert on medical matters or on other matters of expertise. His job, which I think he has done a tremendous job of, is collecting over 20.000 pages of documents and trying to organise them in some way that it would be presentable to a court of law. The report, I understand Your Honour's statement about the direct examination was misleading about the sources of the witness, the statements of witnesses that he used, but his report makes it quite clear and actually quotes the statements, the report itself, that he was not using testimony, but the statements of the witness. Give the Court's request, we can comply with that. I know I saw Mr. Sebire here this morning working on that. He is scheduled to be out of the country on Sunday, he's trying to complete that before he leaves. The one matter that right now is impossible to do, is to look at the updated book of missing persons. We expect that momentarily and I will ask him, I will have Ms. Karper send him an email this morning and ask him if there's any updated word on when that would arrive. I was originally told, I thought, Monday, but now I's told that it may take until next week, but I'll find out about that. As regards to the law on declarations of death, I've already requested an investigator to try to obtain that. I think we will have that by tomorrow, at least in B/C/S. As to Mr. -- As for the documents that Ms. Karper just got, if I could explain the source. I would be asking to have these copies of the document marked and admitted as exhibits. But these documents are a response received from the Republika Srpska liaison officer to a request for assistance from the Office of the Prosecutor. The Office of the Prosecutor requested Republika Srpska to search official records and bank records for signatures of Dr. Stakic. I see that we actually have here three of the pages. The response was longer, but most of the response was simply letters from banks saying they have no record. Three of the pages concern an application for an identity card. And my understanding is this is the application that is kept, the paperwork that is kept by the government office, not the card that the person carries. Excuse me, that's the first page. I believe the second page is -- when I say the first page, it is copied front and back. So the first two pages are the identity document, the second page, I believe, is a driver's licence application. And the third page I don't want to guess what it is. It's indicated on it that it is a request for the issuance for a passport from 1999. The most important of these from our point of view is the first one which contains a Latin script signature that we maintain S Milomir. So I ask that these documents be marked as exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In the meantime, whilst on these documents are disputed, may I ask for some assistance. On the list of material submitted and the expert statement, we find table 1 no doubt with exhibit numbers, table 2 also, but on table 3 there are numerous documents without any court exhibit number. Are these documents already tendered?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: We are trying to obtain the answer. I believe they are. I believe this is the package that we obtained from Judge --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Lindholm. Per Lindholm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, Judge Lindholm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So all these would be included in S --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: 35, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: 35. Fine. Then let's go through the documents we just received. No doubt the Defence may beforehand discuss the documents with their client, if necessary. We would interrupt for this purpose for five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That is acceptable, Your Honour, since we just received the documents at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then the trial stays adjourned until 11.35 a.m. --- Break taken at 11.25 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So, let's first start with the document handed over before the break. We have now to decide on the admission on evidence. The document starting with 01799923, could the OTP please in a language we understand, what this document and apparently following document 924, backside of the same document, what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. This is the identity card filed in the name of Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: This is the identity card file in Bosnia, I think we have heard testimony from Ms. Tabeau about the "maticni broj", the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. personal number and individuals are issued identity cards with that number. This is the file that is kept by the officials for that identity card. And it has the number, "maticni broj" on the, just below the caption at the top, it has a photograph of the individual. It appears in the upper left-hand side of the document, on the first page, the name, and the signature of the person to whom the card is issued appears. Also, it is the second line up on this particular document. This ERN number 01799924 is the backside of that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. And the document was received by?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: This document was received by Suellen Taylor pursuant to an official request for assistance to the Republika Srpska, was handed to the OTP by the liaison pursuant to request --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We have the original or --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Letter, yes. Well, we -- we can give the Court to view the first copy but what is received from the Republika Srpska is a copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Was only a copy. Okay, just to know whether we can work with an original or in this case since it is not necessary. Objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We do, Your Honour, good morning. Our primary objection is twofold. One, the element of surprise. We are constantly being inundated with documents that we believe are in their possession and throughout these proceedings, at least in my opinion, we have been given documents that these that are reported to the OTP a day or two before, but I think the practice that is developing and I understand that we are coming towards the end of the Prosecutor's case in chief, is truly unacceptable to us. We cannot be given documents which purports to go to the witness that today is going to testify before us. His testimony may be incomplete unless he has these documents. There must be a different avenue that we can accomplish this in a more timely fashion. We also received today a signature or signature blocks of two pages of documents which apparently this expert did. Why we weren't given these documents in advance of his expert testimony I don't know, and if I can just show it to the Court, if I may. The Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May we also have these documents, please, a copy. To cut this story short, I think it is necessary to give really a stern warning to the Office of the Prosecutor. We discussed this issue during the break. It is not acceptable and we all have to emphasise this, it is not acceptable the way the Prosecution is working in this case in producing documents. And it can't be a matter of surprise. And only for economical reasons, we decide to proceed nevertheless, on the basis knowing very well that it might be that the witness has to come another time. But we have to start and we can't continue just to waste money and the OTP should be aware that when they in Tribunal costs some thousand dollar, I don't want to quote the exact figure, and, therefore, in balancing the interests and knowing that, no doubt, the accused is aware on the basis of these documents shown to us that he might sometimes somewhere in the past has signed these documents, we shall proceed on this even fragile basis. Therefore these documents 01799923 is admitted into evidence as S283-1 and the following ending with 924 is S83-1. Let's now go to the "karton vozaca". May we hear what it is about and by whom it was received and whether we have only the first copy or an original.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: This is a first copy of what was received from the liaison of the Republika Srpska pursuant to an official request for assistance and it is an application for driver's licence, dated, I believe, March 28th, 1980 -- excuse me, I take that back. Because I see there is also a date of 1995 on the bottom left. I am not sure about the dating, whether the application dates 1980 and these are expiration dates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We are discussing 01799925 and may we ask whether these two documents we are discussing right now have been presented to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: None of the documents received from the request for assistance were presented to the witness. They actually were received over the court break and the witness was not in The Hague at that time and had already completed and submitted his report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The same objections will be on by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Same objections, but if permitted, and I know they admitted the first document S283-1, I did have one other comment on that. That document is a typical document that in the territory for which apparently it was filled out, it requires specifically that it be signed by the authorised personnel as most official documents. We know from our cursory review of that document immediately below Dr. Stakic's purported signature is a blank of the person who should have authorised the signature, so that the documents can be processed and therefore become official. Likewise, we note that there - and I am not sure if this is a copying issue - that there is no stamp of any official seal from the entity that is distributing that. It's my understanding, although limited, based upon information and belief, that the numbers that are placed on the top would have been typically rejected because there is more than one number that is placed -- there is 13 numbers and 13 spaces. When numbers of more than one are put in a single box, it is automatically rejected. And I understand that it goes to weight, but we just want to make a record on the document of our objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you, the following document ending with 925 is admitted into evidence for the reasons given before and the reservations made there under S284. And then it follows the document ending with 926. What is this, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: This is the request for the issuance of a passport dated April 23, 1999 and as with the other two documents it was receive pursuant to the same request of assistance for the liaison of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So 927 would be the backside of 926, correct or?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And once again, we have only copies available.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. And I am asking that the first copy be brought down for the Court to view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think the same objections or additional remarks?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, the same objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: For the same reason and the same reservations given before. 926 admitted into evidence as S285-1, and the next one S285-2. Then, out of the blue during the five minutes' break, we received another set of documents and these are the ones apparently mentioned in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. I believe these are -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: These are included in S235?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No. We have done some research on that. These are the documents received from Judge Lindholm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Were they presented to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: They were presented to the Defence at the same time they were presented to the Office of the Prosecutor, I believe. They have copies of it. These documents we had thought - it is our records -- our records show that they were admitted as J8 but apparently the court records show only the letter from Judge Lindholm was admitted as J8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And consequently we have to go through the documents. And we have all before us table three. And on this basis, we have to continue. May I ask the Defence, is it correct, did you receive these documents earlier?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We did, Your Honour. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Any objections as regards to the admittance into evidence of these documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We do Your Honour, and to preserve our right, we have made an application to have the admittance of those documents, we presumed they were also admitted to be resolved by the appellate court respectfully, the entire search, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, we are aware of this. But nevertheless, for the purposes of the ongoing case and that we can work in the transcript already with the exhibit numbers, please let us do the following work: That we have before us table three and the documents, and the first documents starting with or ending with 732 should go as J8-1. And then continuing 733, -2; 734, -3; 735, -4; 736, -5; 737, -6; 738, -7; 739, -8; 740, -9; 741, -10; 742, -11; 743, -12; 744, -13; 745, -14; 746, -15; 747, -16; 748, -17; 749, -18; 750, -19; 751, -20; 752, -21 753, -22; 754, -23 and then it should end with this document. All in all we have under J8, 23 pages available. Anything else to be discussed before we can start with the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just one thing I want to make clear. I think Mr. Ostojic asked me to clarify it. The Court, Your Honours, have in front of you an updated version of the report. When I say updated, it was pursuant to Your Honours' request that the exhibit numbers be provided in the report to make the report readable or more user-friendly. What we did in order to comply with that, is we asked for an electronic copy of the report, and it should be clear, I don't want anyone to misrepresent, that these numbers, the S numbers that do appear were put in by the Office of the Prosecutor and not by the witness. The witness was given a copy of the version we had last night, and he took that home with him. But he did not write the S numbers in, we did. In the documents that were distributed in the envelope, just to be clear also, the S numbers, when I met with the witness last night, we tried to write in on some of these or hopefully most of these, the S numbers of the documents from which the particular signatures came from. But again, that was done by myself and the witness yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The document you have before you, is it already with the Registry?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: We have it copied for. It will come in through the witness and we have one for the witness as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it the intention of the Office of the Prosecutor to leave this for the explanation of the witness or do you want to explain it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I think it would be better to explain it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: To the witness or by the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: By the witness. It is his working - it is his working - worksheet that he put together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. Then but all the administrative matters are done, this document is tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Both of these documents we would tender or both sheets, we would tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Same objections, Your Honour, as those outlined with documents that were produced today. I think as S280-1, if I am not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. It was the same for the same reasons and with the same reservations. Admitted into evidence as please let me know the following numbers. S286?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: S286 and S287. Where we can read the number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just to make a clarification, I said S280-1. It is actually the objection we would like to incorporate for this document that we made in connection with document S283-1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I understand what you wanted to express and therefore I said with the same reservation. So I think now it is time finally to come to the witness, and I heard that we have an interpreter today so therefore may I ask the usher to escort both persons into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: What we -- I was just speaking with Ms. Karper, what we propose to do if there is no objection from the Bench or from the Defence, we do still have an electronic copy of this report, to add in the numbers, the J8 numbers the Court just mentioned and mark that report as an exhibit into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It would be helpful indeed for the parties and the Bench.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And just to further explain when we added the -- I will wait.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning, both of you. Mr. ten Camp, may I ask you to stand up and to give the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you, please be seated. And then may we please hear the name of the interpreter accompanying you, and also give the solemn declaration. First please your name.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: My name is Sybelle van Hal and I solemnly declare to perform my duties as an interpreter faithfully, independently, impartially, and with full respect for the duty of confidentiality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then the floor is open for the OTP, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. ten Camp, good morning. Could you please, for the record, state your name, and tell us what your current employment is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am C. H. ten Camp. At present I work at the Dutch Forensic Institute in Rijswijk in the Netherlands.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. ten Camp, just to remind you, because interpretation is going on in four different languages, we both have to be careful to speak slowly and to pause between our comments. Between speakers, there should be a significant pause. Sir, you mentioned your employer was the Dutch -- Netherlands Forensic Institute. Can you tell us is that part of a particular branch of the government of the Netherlands?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Dutch Forensic Institute is part of the Ministry of Justice.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Would it be correct or incorrect to say that you work with the police or for the police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Dutch Forensic Institute is not a police laboratory, but it does submit cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Are you part of the prosecution, are you part of the prosecution division?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge I am not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it correct that you actually come under the courts and not the prosecutors' office?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. ten Camp, can you please tell the court what your education experience and training is in the comparison of handwriting in order to offer opinions as to the authorship of the handwriting.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry. I have a technical education, electronic education. I started at the Dutch Forensic Institute in 1978 where I used my knowledge of electronics for research purposes for handwriting research. After about two years I was then trained as a handwriting expert by Mr. Hardy [phoen] who was my supervisor at the time. The programme consisted of on-the-job training, which concluded after several years with an exam. And after I passed that examination, I was qualified to sign reports. Since 1978 until the present, I have worked at the department for handwriting investigation and do comparative handwriting investigations, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. as well as research about classical typewriter print.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can you give us some estimate of the amount of question documents or perhaps I should say, cases regarding question documents in which you have participated in a handwriting comparison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That would be over 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Have you previously testified in courts in the Netherlands or any other country?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Over the past years I have testified before a court, on a few occasions, not often.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. The institute for which you work, the Dutch Forensic Institute, does it have any type of certification from any official body regarding the comparisons of handwriting samples?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Comparative handwriting investigation at the Dutch Forensic Institute, the NFI, is performed according to a method approved by the board of accreditation with corresponding systems of quality assurance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, can you briefly explain to us what techniques are used in making a comparison of a question document with handwriting to a reference sample, in order to offer an opinion as to whether the same person wrote both documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In a comparative handwriting investigation, there are four stages. These four stages are listed in the annex to the report. I can list those stages. They include handwriting analysis, comparison of the observed handwriting characteristics, assessment of the similarities and dissimilarities found and drawing the conclusion. Those are the four phases. Each of those phases can be broken down. I am not sure you want me to go into that amount of detail, but it appears on page one and two of the annex.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps I can just ask you: Did you use techniques outlined in the annex of the forensic handwriting analysis in conducting an analysis at the request of the Office of the Prosecutor of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, can you briefly comment on how your -- well, first -- sorry. Can you tell us the opinions that are offered, that are reached and offered to courts by handwriting examiners, such as yourself? Are these opinions that can be quantified in terms of probabilities or percentages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Results of the comparative handwriting analysis are formulated in a conclusion that indicates to what extent the investigator considers it likely that the questioned handwriting was produced by a certain person. To this end he uses a probability scale.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it possible to assign fixed percentages to that probability scale, such as might be done in a DNA analysis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In handwriting analysis, percentages are not used. Percentages in a conclusion of handwriting analysis would suggest a measure of accuracy that would -- that is not realistic considering the inevitable subjective elements in the comparison process.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, because the Court and counsel for the accused have copies of your annex, I am not going to go through all of the techniques and points that you look at in your analysis, but let me ask you: It does indicate that among the items you look at are margins on the width of the writing, the width of the right and left margins, the top and bottom, you look at spacing between words, spacing between lines, punctuation, and grammar. All of these are among the items that you look at in making your comparison. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In English] Yes, among that. There are some more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Please testify completely in Dutch, just it will confuse the record. I understand you speak English. Sir, can you tell us then, is your ability to reach a conclusion, and particularly the probability of you making an identification of the authorship of a document, is that effected by the quality and quantity of the questioned documents, in other words, the amount of writing and the amount of characters, words, that you have to compare to the reference sample?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The conclusion in handwriting comparison analysis arises, depending on the number of similarities, the quality of similarities and the rarity of similarities. The more material for comparison we have, the better we can perform the comparison. The more the questions -- the more characters in the questioned handwriting, the more opportunities we have for comparison. If the questioned material or the comparison material consists of photocopies or reproductions, that is a limiting factor, because microscopically, some items are no longer visible because of their reproduction quality, as expressed in the conclusion. We always conclude the report, if photocopies have been used with the sentence that you will find in this report as well. The sentence reads that no essential difference may exist between the copy before us or the copy investigated and the original on which the copy is based.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: So photocopies in the questioned material diminishes your probability of making an identification. Does the quality and other factors in the reference material affect your ability to make an identification and can you explain what the ideal is for reference material.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The ideal comparison would comprise the original questioned handwriting, preferably multiple signatures, and an ample quantity of reference signatures of the person concerned in with the original ink deposits. What is also important is that the larger the quantity of the questioned handwriting, the better the opportunities for comparison become.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it correct that in the request of the Office of the Prosecutor you received many documents and were asked to compare a signature on the questioned documents that appears to be S. Milomir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Does the fact that this signature appears to contain only eight letters and two letters, the I and the M are repeated, so six individual letters from the alphabet only, did that affect your ability to make a comparison and the likelihood that you could reach a positive conclusion regarding an identification of the authorship of the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The quantity of writing and number of letters in a signature does come into play at the level of the conclusion. The fewer letters or patterns appear in a signature restricts the level of the conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Going now to your actual work in this case regarding the signature S. Milomir, can you explain to us and illustrate, I believe with a worksheet you brought with us, what you actually did in order to compare the questioned signatures with signatures which were given to you as a reference sample? And first just to be clear on the record, is it correct that table three contains the documents that you used with signatures as a reference sample? Table three in your report on page four.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. In table three there you see the signatures, the reference signatures are included there but the Cyrillic signatures appear in table two. In table three, they are in Latin script. Otherwise, there are a few more in table four, there were reference table signatures in table four in Cyrillic script which means that in effect table one contains the questioned signatures, the disputed signatures.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just received a report, Mr. Ten Camp's report, that we have now added the last exhibit numbers that were just admitted while Mr. ten Camp was waiting to testify. So he does not have it, nor do Your Honours or the Defence, but we have copies to distribute to everyone, and I would also ask that the report be marked as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The next available S number is, please? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number S288, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It is admitted into evidence as S288.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. ten Camp, if you can take a moment to briefly review that and make sure that this is the report that you authored in response to a request from the Office of the Prosecutor, with the exception of the exhibit numbers, the S and J numbers being added by the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You have explained to us that tables two and three and four contain material you used as a reference signatures. Is it correct that table one includes those documents that were given to you as the questioned documents, in other words, you were asked to compare the signatures on table one to see if they were written by the same person that wrote the other documents in tables two, three, and four?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry. We unfortunately, we have to take into account that we started this session at 11.00, and therefore, we have mandatory to make a break now and the trial therefore stays adjourned until 1.00 sharp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I notice that the exhibit, I believe, that was marked as the report does not include the annex that was referred to by Mr. ten Camp. My particular copy is -- I have marked up, but he has one with him. May that be marked as part of the last exhibit, perhaps 289-1 or 288, is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: 288, right. So may it be marked 288-1, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And just for the record, that is the annex labelled from the Ministry of Justice, Netherlands Forensic Institute, forensic handwriting analysis, and it consists of six -- five pages of text.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. ten Camp, I want to turn to the signatures that you were asked to compare, the comparison signatures, that contained what appears to be in Latin script, the signature S. Milomir. Did you prepare a worksheet from the documents that you received in that group of questioned documents? Can you show it to us now on the ELMO, the machine to your right. We will put it on the screen. And can you explain how you put this together.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: For the record, this is Exhibit S286. I'm sorry, my microphone was off. For the record, the exhibit on the ELMO is S286. If we could have a view from a further distance to include more of the document if possible. If the camera could zoom out. Thank you. We all have our own copies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. ten Camp, we are following along with you, but if you could show on the screen how you put this together and how this assisted you in making your analysis.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes I will. At an investigation such as this involving a great many documents, it is convenient when photocopies are made of the signatures concerned and are assembled in an A3 sheet of paper as I have in front of me. That enables to investigator to examine several signatures in a single glance instead of retrieving all of the documents concerned from a box each time. So this is an instrument. The comparison is not based on this document. It is an instrument, but the comparison involves the signatures and the documents concerned. And I will be happy to elucidate this chart. I have marked this one at the top. This is a chart of the documents we received in the first place and they were disputed, questioned. Afterwards, several signatures turned out to be usable as reference material and these are framed in green. The screen is not an excellent quality here, but these are the Cyrillic embodiments of these signature. These five are in Cyrillic script. So on this sheet, they are the reference material. You also see red or orange lines, as you see here and these orange ones mean that the quality of the original documents is not good for performing comparative analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: If I could interrupt you there for a moment. Again, when you use the word "original document" you are referring to the document that you received, whether that was an original signature or a photocopy or whether it was a third or fourth or fifth generation copy, when you used the word "original document" you were referring to what you were given by the OTP as the best copy they had, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I consider what I received from you as the original document. But it could be an umpteenth copy, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Now you mentioned Cyrillic script signatures. Do you, sir, read Cyrillic or are you very familiar with the Cyrillic alphabet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hardly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And you mentioned signatures that were given to you as known or reference signatures. Is it correct that that was information given to you by the Office of the Prosecutor? You were asked to use those as the reference signatures and why they were considered reference or known signatures are not part of your knowledge, you accepted those facts from the Office of the Prosecutor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I am sorry but when I interrupted you, you explained the items with the orange line through them were those whose quality was insufficient for analysis. Can you continue to explain the document you have marked number one S286.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This chart of questioned signatures and a few reference signatures, here I have placed additional information here. You see that there is a letter L or a letter C, and the L reflects the Latin script and the C reflects the Cyrillic script. Otherwise there is an O indication which denotes original ink deposits of the signatures on paper or an R which means a reproduction. You also see the ICTY exhibit numbers, as well as the court numbers but in the latest report I received from you, there are different numbers. So they are not all accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. When you talk about the court numbers, you are referring to last night we put on S numbers and some cases a T number, where there was not an S number. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yesterday evening we did indeed note the S and T numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And when you refer to the ICTY number, you are referring to the eight digit number of the ICTY that was on the -- stamped on each of the documents you received from the Office of the Prosecutor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry. What means T in this connection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: 65 ter, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, can you explain why there are certain -- there are certain yellow highlighting on some of these signatures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the reference signatures, I have compiled a chart of them too, and that's the chart that is marked two with a black circle around it at the top. And the -- I have highlighted in yellow the signatures are the items from the results in my investigation. I am talking about patterns in the questioned signature and similar pattern in the reference material. So this is an instrument for me to see where I found something. It is a tool.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps you could put that worksheet you have marked number two, which we have marked out of your presence as S287, on the ELMO. And before you begin, I note on the top left of this item, number S287, you have again indicated O equals original and R equals reproduction. Is it correct this time when you use the word "original" you are referring to that the document you received from the -- well, I will have you explain it. In this sense, what do you mean by original?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In this case here, I use original in my analysis to indicate that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the signature consists of original ink deposits. The R denotes different deposits that result from a reproduction process.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And again, these are, all the signatures on number two, S287, were signatures which you were instructed by the Office of the Prosecutor to use as a reference material to compare to the questioned documents. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can you explain to us now how you actually made that comparison in this case? And I am asking you to concentrate only on the Latin script questioned documents S. Milomir, your comparison with those with the known documents.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What happens in the comparative analysis is that first we look at signatures that have the same general pattern and you see in the signatures on page one, the questioned signature, that you see certain patterns. And these patterns, as well as the entire design of the signature recurs in the reference material on page two, specifically on at the left of that sheet. To the right, you see signatures legible as Stakic Milomir or only Stakic. That is a different design of signature. In the comparative analysis, we examine the movement sequence of the different patterns of which the signature is comprised as well as the speed and fluency with which they are written and the coordination in the writing movement and with similarities, this means that the similarity should be within the variation of the reference signatures.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, I think one can note that in the questioned document signatures, that there is some variation. Can you comment upon the significance of variations in signatures in various documents? Is this common? Does it have any significance in you in reaching conclusions regarding both the authorship and whether or not a signature is bona fide or -- well, perhaps we will save that until we find those terms. Bona fide and mala fide. First can you comment on the significance of variations.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Every individual places a signature or writes text varies, with respect to the handwriting. In our discipline, we assume that nobody can write exactly the same way, so there is always some variation. And some people's handwriting varies more than other people's handwriting and signature. And in this case, if I examined the signatures questioned, the Latin model on sheet one, I see variations but they are not unusual. The signatures are fluent and as for the signatures in original ink deposits, they appear to have been made fluently. I don't see any characteristics of disguise or other signs of forgery. As for the photocopy signatures, they are a bit harder to gauge. Because not all the details of fluency in the lines and line formation are identifiable any more. But in this case, the variations within the signatures are sufficiently homogenous to compare them with the reference signatures.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. In the interest of time, I am not going to ask you to define bona fide signatures and mala fide signatures, since that is discussed on page four of the annex to your report. But let me just ask you, did you find any evidence that would lead you to a conclusion that the questioned documents on table one included mala fide signatures, that is, an imitation signature, a pseudo imitation signature, a fictitious signature, or pseudofictitious signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the signatures from the documents in table one, I did not find any indications suggesting the forms of signatures you just mentioned so no traces of prior practice, erasure, or signs that they were traced, they are good to the best that I can judge based on the original ink deposits. As for the ink signatures where the quality is insufficient and I have indicated those on sheet one with the orange lines, I cannot judge those. I have disregarded those because I am unable to judge them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: In your worksheets one and two, S286 and S287 we have some portions of the signatures highlighted. Can you just explain why you highlighted these various portions of the signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Once again, these are my notes and I use the highlights to indicate where the forms correspond with the similar forms in the reference material. So that's sheet two. But once again, for me, it is only a tool.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. So we come now to the conclusions that you reached regarding the Latin signatures, that is, the S. Milomir signatures. And I believe that those are listed beginning on page six of your report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The conclusions are on page seven, where I see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I was referring to the results, but let's go right to the conclusions. Perhaps you can explain the difference between the section results and the section conclusions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The results indicate what I found, whether I found similarities or differences or whether I observed other matters of importance for the comparative analysis. You will find all that under the heading, "results."

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Perhaps with the permission of the court, if I could just read the results at least for the Latin script signatures into the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, is it correct that the results in the first paragraph under results that you reached the following conclusions: "Latin script signatures, comparison of question with reference signatures: When comparing the questioned signatures in Latin script, with the corresponding reference signatures, similarities were observed in the order, shape, and proportions of the various graphic elements that can be distinguished within these signatures though there is some variation in the quality of these similarities when looking at the questioned signatures individually. As for the signature on document 0633814, S106, which was treated separately because it is not clear whether it is written in Latin or Cyrillic script, similarities with some of the Latin script reference signatures have been found in the initial part of the signature, interpretable as a letter S. In the remaining part of this signature, however, differences were observed from the Latin as well as from the Cyrillic reference signatures." And were these your conclusions from examining the questioned reference signatures in Latin script and those would be, correct me if I am wrong, those signatures on S286, the first worksheet, table with worksheet one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you please repeat that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Were these the results of your analysis from examining the questioned reference signatures in Latin script, that is, those signatures that are on worksheet number one, that we looked at a few moments ago in Latin script?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I want to move now to the conclusions regarding these Latin script signatures. Starting from the bottom, from the reverse, is it correct that you formed the -- you reached no opinion as to the writer of the reference signatures on document S106, that is 0633814?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct. We did not -- we were unable to reach a conclusions to whether the signature marked S106, whether or not it was written by the writer of the reference signatures material.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And I am trying to locate that signature on your worksheet.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In English] It would help you if you look on your monitor. It is the one on the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, indicate the top right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And for the record, Your Honour, I think this is one that we had previously indicated that we thought was a "Za". Thank you. And also just to make the record easier for everyone to read, I will just read the title of that document in the translation, S106, is entitled "To all commercial and social enterprises, subject, introduction of the permanent operational duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Now, moving on to the next group of opinions regarding a large Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. group of documents. Is it correct, sir, that you reached the conclusion that the writer of the reference signatures possibly wrote the questioned signatures on the following documents, and you list them. I am only going to read into the record the S numbers. S68, S64, S175, S71, S72, S82, S70, S77, S66, S178, S179, S172, S75, and S69. Was that your conclusion regarding these documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: In the annex that you attached, you explained what the conclusion "possibly" means. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: The corrected -- your conclusion possibly, and I am reading from page 4, the third paragraph, second sentence, "the conclusion possibly means that the findings of the examination are consistent with the proposition that the disputed material was produced by the suspect in question. But that no combination of writing characteristics typical of the suspect was noted to warrant it conclusion probable or stronger." Do you agree that that is a correct definition of the significance of your conclusion that these documents were possibly written by the author of the reference documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it correct then that there is a significant difference between a conclusion that you can offer no opinion and a conclusion that the writing was possibly written by the suspect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is there a difference then between a conclusion of no opinion, and a conclusion that the suspect possibly authored the questioned documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there is a difference. In an analysis, we were unable to give an opinion, it is usually because of several factors. And the conclusion possibly means that there are some points of similarity that we have observed, which, while not sufficient to justify the conclusion probably, there is a difference between the conclusion "no opinion" and "possibly."

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Finally, you reached the conclusion, the writer of the reference signatures probably wrote the questioned signature on document P0038333, that is S173. Can you show us on the worksheet where that document S173, that signature appears?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the chart number one, you will see at the right, at the extreme right, a reproduction of this signature. And this signature on the original document was there in original ink deposits. So that provides a stronger basis for comparison.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: For the record, perhaps that document could briefly be put on the ELMO. I have a copy of it. That is the document regarding the signatures for the SDS bank account and I would just like the witness to identify which of the signatures that appear on that page that he used as the questioned signature.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is this signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Indicating what appears to be S. Milomir, below what appears to be Dr. Kovacevic's signature. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Now, I want us to go over to the last exercise that you did, and that was making a comparison between certain Latin script signatures. And is it correct that we discussed last night that there may have been some miscommunication regarding the exact instructions for that task?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: But, can you please tell us the instructions as you understood them, what you understood, and what exercise you went through in making that comparison, the conclusions of which are under item number three of conclusions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I examined was whether the signatures as they are listed here, I examined whether they contained similarities to the two signatures listed at the bottom of the text. I assumed the -- that the largest number of signatures were written by one person. Based on this assumption, I then compared those signatures with signatures S179 and S172. And I conclude that this group of signatures was probably written by the person who placed the signatures S179 and S172 as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And for the record, Your Honour, I believe Your Honours have these documents before you, but S179 was the document entitled in the translation, "Supplement to the minutes," and there was a signature on the lower right of that document. And the translation indicates the authenticity of the statement as certified by, and then the signature - excuse me - then typed Milomir Stakic and then a signature. And I could -- I don't know if it is necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could it please also be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The colour copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, please. And also then if you could take up at the same time, S172.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can you show us, first showing you S179, which is the signature that you used in making this comparison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's this signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Indicating again what appears to be S. Milomir and the signature on the right-hand side of the document. And now if you could be shown S172 which is entitled for the record in the translation, record sheet handwritten and what appears to be "Stakic Milomir, attended the Prijedor Municipality Assembly meeting on," handwritten "04/01/1991" and it is printed signature and a signature below that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can you point out the writing you used for the signature in comparison in this exercise on S172.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is this signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I am finished with the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. ten Camp, you have discussed a little bit about the craft of handwriting analysis, and what you do, and you have discussed the limitations on the present exercise based upon the quantity and quality of both the questioned and reference documents that you have received. In your experience in working, is it correct that you have worked on many cases where the authenticity of documents is in question, is an issue for the courts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And is it correct that handwriting analysis is one tool that can be of assistance in determining authenticity but that other factors, such as location where documents were found or the source of the documents, the circumstances under which they were found, even the contents of the documents and other surrounding circumstances all affect authenticity but are outside of the science that you practice of anaylsing the handwriting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Comparative handwriting analysis, I am talking about the Netherlands in this case, comparative handwriting analysis figures in penal cases as well as civil cases and is certainly one of the tools, in combination with other tools, such as the findings from investigation to convince the court whether somebody has or has not written something. You mentioned other cases. We don't deal with other factors concerning this. We use the handwriting primarily with respect to the document and possibly the content of the text. But we have somebody who is specialised in text analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. ten Camp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. May we proceed with the cross-examination immediately?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. ten Camp. My name is John Ostojic and together with Branko Lukic we represent Dr. Milomir Stakic. I am going to ask you a series of questions here today and I would appreciate, to the extent possible, that you clarify some points for me. My first question to you involves the probability scale that is identified within your report and the annex that is attached to your report. Is it correct that in the field of forensic handwriting comparative analysis, examiners utilise different probability scales, as Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. opposed to one probability scale as identified in your annex?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right. Abroad, outside the Netherlands, there are experts or institutions which use other formulas as to the probability scale. But regarding the NFI, this is the one we use. But you are right in saying what you say.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so that I understand it, how do I determine, as a lay person, which probability scale I should utilise, one from a different country or the one that is offered by the Netherlands?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know either.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with what the probability scale is for examiners who study and are considered to be experts within the field of comparative handwriting analysis in the United State?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I read something about it, indeed, and I have met with colleagues who work in America in the field, but I don't know exactly how they work out their formulas.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I can just direct your attention to page 4 of your annex, specifically III.II.I, which is the probability scale. I have a couple of questions on that, if you don't mind on that. I am just waiting for the translation in the different languages to get caught up. Within this probability scale, there seems to be six specific levels that can be utilised by an examiner such as yourself in conducting this comparative analysis, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The opinion of possibility and the opinion of no opinion, is that a hybrid between, again looking at the probability scale, is that a hybrid between the levels of probably and probably not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you mind repeating the sentence or your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We know that within the probability scale that you utilised, there are six specific levels for purposes of reaching a conclusion. In addition to that, as the article suggests and as you have opined here today, there are two additional levels, at least, identified "possibly" and "no opinion". My question to you, sir, is, is it fair to place those two additional categories the "possibly" and "no opinion" and consider them as a hybrid in between the six recognised levels, namely, probability and probably not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you place it, sir, the two that you have just distinguished for us, "possibly" and "no opinion," within any category of those six levels that you identified in the probability scale?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are various degrees that I mentioned here in the scale. The concept of "possible" and "no opinion" do not belong in the scale. That's why we provide a separate explanation of what we mean by those concepts and how we reach them but it is not possible to place them within the various degrees of the probability scale.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fully understood. Thank you. With respect to the category "possibly" that you reference, it states that within this article that "no combination," and I am emphasising the word "no," so "no combination of writing characteristics typical of the suspect was noted to warrant the conclusion probable or stronger," correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so that I understand when it states "no combination of characteristics are noted" that means absolutely none, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: When I ask you a couple of questions that, specifically, combination of characteristics with respect to your third conclusion and opinions in this case, but to try to somewhat logically go through it, we will go back to some questions that I have, generally speaking, and then we will go back to the specifics of your report. Okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Generally speaking, the way I read your report, your first project was to take table number one, which I think have been referenced as the disputed signatures, and you compared it to table number three, which were the so-called recognised signatures correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In English] Yes, that is right, but also with table two and table four, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, maybe you could explain it to me. I thought your first task, if you will, was to compare the Latin script, the Latin signatures as they are identified in the category of disputed signatures, identified on table one, and not to include any of the Cyrillic signatures, whether disputed or recognised, as you called it, and simply compare the Latin signatures disputed with the Latin signatures recognised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, sir. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, there is no need. Now, within your conclusions, if we can just direct your attention to that, and I have it on page six. I am not sure what copy you are necessarily working with. The Latin script signatures, you have placed them when you made this comparative handwriting analysis, in three categories, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which page do you find that on?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I have it under page six but I'm not really sure. There are many copies. It is the first paragraph of your conclusions. I think the one you are looking at is a modified -- is not the same one I am looking at. Page seven of one copy and page six of these other two copies. They are all the same, basically I think.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On page seven, I have the conclusions, in my copy. Do you want to speak about that page?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am going to ask you a question specifically for your first conclusion which deals with the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone. Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, I am going to ask you questions specifically in connection with that, the Latin signatures disputed versus recognised. That being your first task, you reach a conclusion with respect to those documents that you analysed and reviewed, you came up with three separate categories, correct? Let me walk you through it. One the category of probably, the other category of possibly and the other category of no opinion, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, with respect to the documents that you reviewed in making this comparative analysis from disputed and recognised signatures, is it fair to say that there is only one document in that entire set of documents that you analysed that you could, with any certainty, conclude that it falls within the recognised six levels as identified in your annex and it falls within the category of "probably." Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That's the only one where I said it was probable.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Within the category of probable, is there any -- strike that. Within -- thank you. Within the level of probably, are there any degrees to which you can quantify for us that it had a higher probability or a lower probability or do you have no opinion in that regard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't tell you whether it is more probable or not because you have the various sequences. I can only say it is probable. I can't say anything more about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But can you give us an opinion as to whether or not that signature that appears on S173 of the first section of your conclusions, whether it was -- strike that. I apologise, Mr. ten Camp. Now, with respect to the second section of your conclusions on paragraph number one, you conclude that those items listed and the reference signatures, possibly was the conclusion, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, the Office of the Prosecutor asked you a couple of questions Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. regarding your, respectfully, narrow focus of documents for purposes of authenticity. Would it be of any interest to a handwriting comparative examiner, such as yourself, to know whether there has been any claims as to whether or not the documents that you are being asked to review are in some fashion suspect?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Objection. Irrelevant to this case, because there has been no evidence that they are suspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It is a hypothetical question. We are not saying that they are and we wouldn't -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You may answer, I believe.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you mind repeating the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I will try, thank you. Does it matter to a -- generally speaking, sir, would it matter to you as a handwriting comparative examiner to know whether there is any underlying dispute as to whether the documents given to you, specifically within this second category of conclusions number one, that they are in some way alleged to be suspect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For me, as an examiner, it doesn't make any difference whether a document is a questioned document or whether it is another document. I only look into comparing the signatures or the writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: These documents that you identify as possibly being written by an individual, should they not, sir, retain their identification of being documents that are at least, in your view, based upon your appendix, not considered probable and not even considered within the six levels that you identify in your probability scale?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I am sorry. Objection because I don't think it is an understandable question. At least I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I worked on it. I can restate it if the Court wishes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please restate your question. I think the direction is would it be identical with probably not as the next category.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But if I may just ask another question in that vein just to clarify. Would you take, sir, those signatures that appear in this category of possibly written by a suspect and when you compare the signatures within that category, would it be a failure to conclude that any of these signatures, with respect to themselves would be able to somehow make the probability scale that you attach in your appendix, and specifically, I will direct your attention to the conclusions, sir, that you reach on paragraph three of your conclusions, wherein, in my interpretation at the very least, you took those possibly written signatures, and compared two of them with the remaining ten or so, and concluded that there was a probability that those within themselves are somehow signatures by a suspect?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I have the same objection, unless the witness understands it. The question is, would it be a failure to conclude, etc. I don't understand what a failure to conclude is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, in addition, I would ask the Defence not to do the typical German mistake with all these long sentences. If you could have some short interpretable sentences, it would facilitate all our work.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. ten Camp, you list these possible signatures. Can you tell us more probably true than not, whether the signatures that appear on this document page six, under the second indentation of conclusion number one, can you tell us, more probably than not, whose signatures those are, based upon your comparative analysis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The signatures, the reference signatures, that is, are possibly written by the one who has written the questioned signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I understand that is your opinion. Can you, sir, based upon a reasonable degree of certainty tell us whether or not, I know possibly you can, but can you tell us upon a reasonable degree of certainty as to the probably or not whether those are the signatures of the person identified as being those of the recognised signator?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I maintain what I said. The signatures to be found under the first conclusion, namely, that they are possibly wroted -- written by those who signed the reference signatures. I maintain that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And you can't give us anything stronger other than possibly, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Then in the third category within the conclusions of section one on page six of your report, you have one document that you have referenced, that you have no opinion on, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In English] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, I would like to discuss it if I may the second section of your conclusions, the Cyrillic script signatures. And I would like for you, sir, to look at table number two of the signatures that were photocopied and categorised. It's on your right-hand side. The two with the circle in the middle of the page. Yes, sir. Yes, do we have it? Yes, do we have it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am looking.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On that document which I think is marked as S287, on the lower right-hand side, there is a Cyrillic signature that appears. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which one? Do you mean this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, the lower right-hand side. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With respect to that signature, I have a couple of questions. One is: The reproduction seems to be, at least for my purposes, adequate. Do you agree or disagree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Rather good, reasonably good.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I agree with you, not that it matters, but if we could have the actual exhibit, S225, Your Honour, placed on the usher --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: On the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Placed on the ELMO by the usher. Thank you, Your Honour. My apologies to the usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And now, sir, just so the record is clear, we have Exhibit S255, which seems to be the signature portion of the document that refers or is identified in S287, lower right-hand corner, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the signature on S225.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, two questions in connection with this document, if I may. Why on table three in your report under that specific exhibit number S225, you state that the quality of reproduction is poor, when in fact, we are in agreement, it looks pretty good. How do I reconcile that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure whether I have seen this document or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could Defence counsel please indicate in which table --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Table three, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Table three.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It is under -- would you like the ICTY Exhibit number which is I think they're ERN numbers or?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So you make reference to page three of the report, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour. Three lines from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I am sorry, page three of the report, three lines -- page three of the report I have has only three lines, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No. We have so many reports --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You are making reference to the materials submitted, page three. There, on the third last line, S225.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just for easy reference, because there's three copies that are going -- apparently being utilised. It is on table three. And if we look at table three, it is the third from the bottom on table three.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, but opposed to the results, we are now Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. working with the material submitted on page three of the same document?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
