utterances.text: Mr. ten Camp, I just wanted to see how we can reconcile this. Why do you identify under this document which has been identified as S225, why do you state that it is poor reproduction quality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At any rate I did not look, I did not examine this reproduction.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Why not, if I may ask? If your second task was to make a comparative analysis of the Cyrillic scripts as you identified in your report, did you omit to use Exhibit S225?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I used a similar document, but not this one. I cannot, therefore, tell you -- I can't tell you out of my head what was the quality of the reproduction of the document that I used.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: By looking at Exhibit 225 now, and looking on Exhibit 287 which is your chart with the two in the middle of it, you have or someone has a little arrow on that document, do you know what that means, on the bottom right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It means that when I first saw the document, I didn't know exactly whether I was to deal with the document that was left of the document of the one that was right, on the right-hand side of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think I just recently and Judge Vassylenko identified the problem. Because we can find copies of the same document twice. If the usher could please present to the witness and on the ELMO the documents we see ERN number 195472, where the signature is readable, and 191347 where it is evidently not readable. This is one copy which apparently is the one used on this comparative sheet number two, and then opposed to this, please show us the other. On the right-hand side, please. The signature on the right -- yes. Opposed to this, this indeed is a poor quality.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I agree with Your Honour, but if I can just be permitted a little latitude to just explain --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No doubt. I am just trying to find out why the expert came to the conclusion of poor quality.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: On the sheet that, Mr. ten Camp, you prepared with the signatures, specifically Exhibit 287, with the two in the middle of it, you utilised the copy, the good reproduction, right? I mean you copied it, you catalogued it on the lower right-hand side of your exhibit, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as this signature is concerned, I received it as reference material, however, I was trying to explain to you that first I didn't know exactly which signatures I was to analyse in the left lower corner. Because there was one left and another one in the right-hand side. So in the beginning when I received the document, that wasn't known to me and that's why I put this remark in. Because in the left-hand corner, the reproduction is pretty poor, and as to the right-hand signature, that seemed to be reference material from Mr. Stakic, that is of rather good quality. But I think that if I mention poor reproduction, that relates to the whole document and also to the left-hand side signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, the document that you identified here, and have placed in the purported recognised signatures of Dr. Stakic, that document, and believe you me, Mr. ten Camp I don't understand to purport to know the Cyrillic script any better than you do, but that signature and document seems to identify a Milorad Stakic and not Dr. Milomir Stakic. If, in fact, as an expert, had you analysed the complete name, both last name and first name, I think you will note that there are other characters, namely letters, that appear in this signature, that do not appear in any of the other signatures that you have cataloged here on S287.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is no question on that statement by counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It is indeed a statement and no reason to answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. ten Camp, help me out with this. I mean, you're the expert, shouldn't you have been able to, at least, identify that the signatures don't even come close to the signatures that are identified by the OTP as being recognised or even those that are identified as disputed, if it is true that the signature that appears on S225 is that of another individual?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't ask whether the -- which was the reference and which was the questioned material.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the witness repeat the question -- his answer, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. ten Camp, there was a request that you repeat your answer. The interpreter did not get it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I received material, I ask what is the reference material and what is the questioned material. When I receive reference material of which I think the signature looks different from the other one, then it is quite possibly a variation of a different signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...of what we are discussing, the usher was kind enough to present two documents of the compilation of documents admitted into evidence as S235 and, of course, my question goes to the OTP. Which of these documents were, indeed, provided to the expert? Because none of the ERN numbers within S235 can be read on table three, page three of this document -- of this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Well, what I have, Your Honour, is that S225 is the ERN number 02017198. And that was what you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, but you can see and apparently there is a flaw with all these documents that there are mentioned -- it is mentioned in the last column, two copies. But we have only one ERN number in the second column.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: If Your Honour recalls, these are items that were taken from Dr. Stakic at the time of the arrest, by Mr. O'donnell. The documents Mr. O'donnell indicated, he prepared a form, an IFF form, and the documents were given to the Evidence Unit. When we asked for the search warrant for the order to have the Detention Unit searched at that location, these documents had not yet received an ERN number. The ERN was put on through the efforts of Suellen Taylor throughout the course of this trial. So we did have copies and the court and the Prosecutor had copies and apparently both were provided to the witness without the ERN number and with the ERN number. And my recollection could be wrong, but I believe that Mr. ten Camp was first provided with the documents when we first had them, without the ERN number. And then either Mr. Dupas or Mr. Dupas would have provided to him, one of the investigators, a copy with the ERN number. That is my best belief of how he received two copies of the exact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So it seems to be undisputed that this readable document where we have a copy on this comparative sheet number two, was the basis for the work of the expert and no doubt this was one of the documents seized during the arrest of Dr. Stakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: That's correct, that it was this document. The quality of the copy that he got, because we are all dealing with copies, first the item would be printed from key file, which is where it is scanned, and then likely copied to give him one. I cannot tell you what the quality of that copy was he received -- either of the copies that he received. Perhaps I can explain further. Maybe I shouldn't, but, Mr. Ten Camp, I believe has with him -- he first received copies and then he received actual - he could correct me during his testimony - he received the best copies. He received the items from the Evidence Unit that we had. So he would have for many of these documents, the actual item, chain of custody from the Evidence Unit. But again, we never had -- or the original of this document or the first copy that the OTP had was one of those returned to the Detention Unit, which they indicate they returned to the accused. Mr. ten Camp --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Nevertheless, it seems to be quite clear. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Because when we have an in-depth look on this comparative sheet, we can -- it is difficult, but, indeed we can identify in parenthesis, 02017198, that was ERN number given to this document and though there should be no longer any doubt what document was the basis for the work of the interpreter. And we only know that there was an additional given of this copy of this document given to the expert which indeed has had poor quality. Probably this is the reason why it is mentioned here was poor reproduction quality, but, of course, it is not for you to go on with questions related to this indeed readable signature and the meaning for the outcome of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. ten Camp, thank you. Sorry for the brief discussion. With respect to this third conclusion. We've now completed conclusion number one and that is the Latin scripts being compared or analysed by you, namely, the recognised versus disputed text, as identified, and now we've gone through the Cyrillic script. And the third conclusion, sir, or the third category that you examined, seems to be based on several assumptions. In fact, on the first sentence under the category number three of conclusions, you state that you are making an assumption that the following signatures were all written by one person.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I did indeed make that assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Tell me how extensive the assumption was if you relate it to the six level categories within the probability scale.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I am sorry, Your Honour. I don't see how the witness can answer a question. He said he assumed it was true. I don't see how the probability scale is at all relevant to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, probably the question may be rephrased, whether or not one could use also this six levels of probability for this number three category.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Would the witness be kind enough to answer the Court's question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me. Would you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I can restate it. I tried to just facilitate it. When you made the assumption, Mr. ten Camp, that the signatures were all written by one person under section three of your conclusions, did you utilise, in formulating your assumptions, any of the levels within the probability scale that we have been discussing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So it is fair to state that your assumption was not that there is high probability that these signatures are all the same, or that there was probability that the signatures are all the same, or that the signatures were probability bordering uncertainty, correct, none of those three?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was an assumption, and I stated in the report that it was an assumption, and in the report I have also stated that the signatures are highly consistent, combined with natural variations. That's why we made that assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What you are doing is, sir, when you took all those signatures that you identified under category conclusion number three, you analysed those signatures, and you found that those signatures possibly can fall within the recognised signatures, when you made that comparative analysis, and now in essence for category three, you take those same possible signatures, and you withdraw two from the sample given by the OTP, and have merely compared two of the possible signatures you opine on section one, and conclude on section three that those two probably are the same of those that previously you identified as being possible, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first time I identified possibly with the reference material of Mr. Stakic and in this case, I explored a group of questioned signatures. So perhaps the first time in the first analysis, has nothing to do with the probable finding in the second investigation, second analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So it is not logical, or it is not a logical extension to state that signatures that you have identified as not falling within the category of the probability scale, and are merely possibly related to the recognised signatures, how is it logical to identify any of those signatures as having any probability or be able to fall within any of the six categories in the probability scale? I am sorry, I am just not following it logically.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I performed two investigations. One investigation of the questioned Latin signatures and the reference material for reference signatures. That was part one of the analysis, and that revealed that one signature had probably been authored by the author of the reference material in the other signatures, below, this was possibly the case for them. Next the question was asked and that concerns the third analysis, which is entirely separate. The question was whether I could compare two signatures with several other signatures. And based on that, I concluded that the group of signatures indicated on your page six and my page seven, that they were probably authored by the person who authored S179 and S172.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just a couple more. I know we are pressed for time, and then I can conclude my cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think we have to continue later and we are really already 15 minutes overtime now. I am awfully sorry, but we have to make a break now until 3.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please continue with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. ten Camp, just a couple of questions on the probability scale, if I may. Have you ever, sir, worked with a scale which includes categories of "with certainty" and then another category that is identified commonly with the field of forensic handwriting analysis, "absolute certainty" and the additional two converse to those two levels are "certainty not" and then "absolutely not." Are you familiar with those categories?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The witness has already answered that question stating that this scale is the one used in the Netherlands and that abroad one uses different scales, so it doesn't help.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. ten Camp, may I ask you when you analyse documents for the justice institute or your employer, are the documents utilised in both criminal -- strike that. Are the issues presented to you in both criminal and civil proceedings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mainly criminal proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And is it correct then that in those criminal proceedings you also utilised this annex attached as an exhibit and it is these six probability scales that you utilise in the criminal proceedings, as opposed to another probability scale?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In all comparative handwriting analysis that we perform, this annex is added to the report we issue with this list of degrees of probability.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: One final area if I may cover with you. During your direction examination, you testified regarding the following, and I think you stated in summary, if I may, sir, that there were few characters or letters that an examiner has to evaluate, the more restrictive the level of conclusion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And in this case, obviously or at least -- maybe I shouldn't say obviously. Strike that. In this case --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please speak closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In this case, sir, you actually have very few characters to deal with correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Enough for the conclusions I reached.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I agree and thank you for that. However, so that I understand, if the fewer characters or letters that an examiner has to evaluate, the more restrictive the level of the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. conclusion, to what extent are the conclusions that you provided us restricted or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The number of characters or elements of which a signature is comprised is sufficient to reach a conclusion, as I mentioned here, probably and even most probably if we had had more reference signatures or more originals of them. So the number of letters or elements of which the signatures comprised, especially the Latin version, would have enabled a stronger conclusion as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. ten Camp, on behalf of the Defence, we want to thank you for your clear report and your testimony here. We appreciate it. Thank you, sir, very much. Dank u wel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. And you're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Any additional questions by the OTP, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I have two areas to cover. And I can only think of the first one and perhaps I will cover that and then think of the second.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: On the second worksheet S287 you were asked a line of questions regarding the signature on the lower right which is from the document S225, is it correct that you did not use this signature in your analysis as one of the reference signatures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In comparing the signatures in Cyrillic script, this signature hardly came into play.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: So would it be correct that this signature S225, did not affect the conclusions you reached about the Cyrillic, and particularly, about the Latin signatures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The signature S225 was one that I used only for comparison with signatures in Cyrillic script, and this signature hardly affected the conclusion I issued. As for the signatures in Latin script, this signature is hardly usable because it contains shapes that do not appear in the signatures in Cyrillic script.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise. Excuse me. That appear in the signatures in Latin script was what I meant to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. The last area I wish to cover concerns the third conclusion in your report on the last items under "conclusions" in which you talked about comparing the signatures of the questioned documents and those are all those signatures are contained on worksheet number one, S286. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you please indicate once again which signature on worksheet one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: My question was, in section number three, you compared S68, S64, S175, S71, S72, and S82, and actually as I am reading that, we see that you are writing them in the order that they appear in the worksheet starting from the left hand column working down and now to the middle column S70, S77, S76 and then excluding again the copies that you found were too poor to contribute to the analysis, S178 and S75, and you compared those to the signatures -- well, first you looked at those as a group. You were asked some questions about that on your cross-examination. I would like to compare those signatures within worksheet number one, the questioned documents with your initial exercise where you compared them with the reference signatures on worksheet number two. And I am concentrating only on the Latin signatures, which I believe appear on that worksheet. Is it correct that on the left-hand side of the worksheet number two you have all the signatures that appear to be S Milomir and on the right-hand side as the name of Stakic in different forms, Stakic Milomir, simply Stakic, Stakic M.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The questions that you have asked, could you please ask them individually because I have lost track of the flow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Would it be correct to say, state first, on worksheet number two that you have separated on the reference signatures, the signatures that appear to be S. Milomir on the left-hand side of that document, and the other forms of the signature of Stakic on the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the left of the page, there are indeed signatures of which the realisation varies with respect to the signature on the right side of this form. And in comparing them, I used both designs, both models. But there are two or three models that appear on sheet number two.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. I am sorry, but I am trying to ask just a question leading up to another question, and I am not doing it very well. Let me try again. Just the signatures that are S. Milomir, is it correct that these are grouped on the left-hand side of your worksheet, as a first step?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it correct that in those reference signatures, S. Milomir, you did not have any originals, these are all reproductions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The signatures on the left-hand side of the page, that is, S. Milomir, they are all photocopies or reproductions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if we go to the questioned documents, the group that you were comparing, doing an internal comparison of in your third conclusion, is it correct that if we look at those questioned signatures and eliminating those that you put the orange line through because of the poor reproduction, that we have in the first column starting from the left, one, two, three, four, five, originals; in the second column we have five originals; in the third column we have one original; and in the very last column we have one original S. Milomir signature, which is the third box up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Giving what you told us earlier about the difficulty and the advantages of comparing originals as opposed to copies, did this assist you in making this internal comparison of the signatures on worksheet one, did the fact that they were many original signatures on this worksheet make it easier for you to make an internal comparison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That did not necessarily facilitate the comparison, but it did enhance the efficiency, because you can see more in such a signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. ten Camp. May I first point out that the Bench is extremely grateful for your expertise given and, in such a short period of time, from domestic jurisdiction I am not acquainted to receive this report in such a very short period of time. But let me go into three details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: When you draw your conclusions, do you make a distinction between handwritten text and signatures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not ordinarily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Make reference to this sheet called "forensic handwriting analysis," page four where on the top III.II, drawing the conclusion, you find III.II.I, "handwritten text," opposed to III.II.II "signatures". What is the reason for this distinction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because signatures are usually brief written expressions that, at least in the Netherlands, are largely unreadable. And they may involve other problems because especially signatures are subject to forgery, whereas handwritten texts usually are not. That's why we devote additional attention to the signatures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So is it a correct understanding to state that you categorised the words before you as a handwritten text opposed to a signature because it is closer to the categories of handwritten text than of signatures you are acquainted with here in the Netherland?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Signatures containing elements that are recognisable as letters are can be compared as texts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The second point, it was already mentioned several times, but to be quite clear, on the same page it reads, the conclusion "no opinion" indicates that a comparative handwriting examination could not be carried out. Is this word "no opinion" equal with the words "niet bruikbaar" in your working sheets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No that's not completely identical. The statement "not usable" means that the quality is insufficient to perform any analysis, whereas with "no opinion" if you continue reading in the annex, you see exactly what "no opinion" means on page four. "Not usable" is a remark to me personally to indicate that the signature does not lend itself to a worthwhile comparison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. I was just quoting from this paragraph three. So, therefore, we have two different categories, "niet bruikbaar," and no opinion, because for other reasons an examination could not be carried out. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The statement "not usable" is not a conclusion. It is not done a conclusion from handwriting analysis. I evaluate whether a signature is usable if the quality is that poor, then I can't use it at all, it is not a conclusion of the handwriting analysis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this. And then let's go one step forward. The Defence quoted already from the part of the definition of the conclusion "possibly" where it states "no combination of writing characteristics typical of the suspect was noted to warrant the conclusion probable or stronger," but the definition starts, "the conclusion possibly means that the findings of the examination are consistent with the proposition that the disputed material was produced by the suspect in question." No doubt you used the two parts for your conclusion of this definition.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me. Would you please repeat the question. Or at least perhaps you could decompose it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I am making reference to paragraph three under III, to drawing the conclusions that you find the definition in sentence two, what it means, that a conclusion is possible. And I, preparing the next question, wanted to make reference to the first part that you, in addition to the second part of the definition you also based your conclusion "possibly" on this part of the definition saying that the findings of the examination are consistent with the proposition that the disputed material was produced by the suspect in question. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May we now turn to working sheet one and two. Could you please give us the reason why on certain parts of signatures you highlighted parts of the signature in the yellow colour? What is the reason for this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As you already said on page two or on sheet number two, we see reference signatures and on sheet one we see mainly questioned signatures. When I compare, I examined the shapes that correspond with each other and extract the information from those shapes, and if they correspond, then I consider this a similarity. What I have highlighted in yellow, those are the references where I have found the similarities in the reference materials. So it is a tool for me to highlight in yellow where I find the similarities or the points of similarity. It was not my intention for these results to be used at this session but I did not object to their request from the officer that they be used. But these highlights that I have added are rather personal. They are purely a tool for me to see where I found what.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would it be correct to state that this work was done for the purpose to come to the conclusion "no opinion," "possible," or "probable"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. The third area of your conclusions in the report may I first ask: We have a column of documents in conclusion number three. And before we can read on this assumption that the following signatures were all written by one person when we find this column. When comparing this column with the column under number "1," I was surprised to find, for example, the first document where you came to the conclusion "probably," not included in number three. And the other way around, from the first column, the last, the second last and the third last where you came to the conclusion "possibly," are not included in column three. Why this distinction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your first question as to why document S68 on the top column was rated as "possible" and as "probable" in the bottom column is because I compared the documents in the top column with other signatures than the documents in the bottom column. That's the answer to your first question. And with the second question, I need to take a look and see why numbers S172 and S75 do not appear in the second column, that was your question. Was that your question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: S179, S172, S69, and S173 do not appear in the column under point three.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I may repeat, S179, S172, S69, and you mentioned one more.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 173. That one. I will take a look. The signature S179 in the top column, I used that for comparison with the bottom column, because you see in the two lines beneath the bottom column you see S179 indicated. So I did use that in my comparison and the same holds true for S172. As for S173, I don't know why that signature is not in the bottom column, but I think I omitted it because that signature has already been attributed to the other reference signatures with the conclusion of Mr. Stakic. And that leaves one, that is S69. S69, 4309. I have got it over here. At S69, at the top of page seven, I wrote that the quality of the reproduction was insufficient to perform good comparison, that's why we omitted it. I described that there to be [In English] might be left out because of its poor reproduction quality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification. The next question goes to the OTP. What about the additional material you provided early this morning before the witness entered courtroom? Do you want to include this material? Do you regard it as necessary?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I didn't include it for two reasons: First, because it was just provided to the Defence, it wouldn't be fair to them; second, because I had not provided it to the expert, and it obviously would take him some time; but third and probably most important, it itself is another photocopy. If I had an original, I certainty would have liked to have shown that to him. But it would just be another photocopy S. Milomir signature to be added to the reference material, and I don't think it is of better quality than the photocopies we already have and the reference material on the second worksheet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask the Defence, do you agree that it is not necessary to ask for an additional comparative analysis on the basis of these additional four photocopies you contested this morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, we agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. May I then ask Judge Fassi-Fihri do you have any additional questions? Judge Vassylenko? No additional questions. Well then it remains for me to thank you very very much for this fast and exhaustive work, and indeed, did assist us in coming once again one step closer to the truth. Thank you. You are excused. May the usher please escort the witness and the translator, once again, also my thanks to the so-called chicotte interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Before the witness packs it up, we did ask if he could leave his copy of the annex so we could mark that as an exhibit. I don't think the Registry has that. We gave it a number earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We gave it a number -1. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We then can proceed in one language less, which I hope will facilitate the remaining period of time. But may I first hear from the OTP what is now finally envisaged for tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Tomorrow we do have the civilian witness, however, that witness is arriving tonight. It would be our request to have time to speak to that witness tomorrow morning, because the witness I think will not be at the hotel until probably after 10.00. If we could start with her at 11.00. If Your Honours would like to use the time before that, I have a couple of suggestions. I wasn't clear yesterday or I am not clear at the moment, Your Honour mentioned the Judges' questions for Mr. Sebire. He could be here tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Indeed, we can start then with Mr. Sebire notwithstanding that it remains for Mr. Ostojic to complete the cross-examination later, because for tomorrow, he is excused on the basis of mandatory dates abroad. So, therefore, it would be -- it would facilitate our work if we could start at 9.30 with Mr. Sebire, and may I ask what about incoming documents? Do you -- do we receive all the documents forming the basis of other reports and not yet tendered today? This would be the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. On the worksheet that was offered, I don't think we marked that as an exhibit. The gazette-ed worksheet. There were some documents that were not in evidence that Your Honour indicated, for completeness, we should do that. We have those here today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could it please be distributed so we could prepare for tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I would also indicate that Ms. Karper is checking now with Mr. Corin, the author of the linguistic or document analysis report, he returned to the Netherlands yesterday or returned to work today in any event. He is finalising his report. I spoke to him this morning. I hope we can give a copy right now before we leave court, to the Defence of his report. Again, I would ask them once they read it and Your Honours get a copy, it would be my intention to proffer the report as an exhibit without calling Mr. Corin, unless that's objected to. Ms. Tabeau has indicated her report would be available Monday. The updated version of the book of missing persons, the latest information is that it will be available in electronic form. I am not quite sure what electronic form that means. I am not sure if it's text that can be printed, or if its a database, but we'll find out when we receive it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would it be possible that we receive a list 7 for these documents just recently obtained?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: That should take about ten seconds more and then we will have list 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It serves the purpose that we can, if the OTP needs additional time for the preparation of the witness or proofing of the witness, that we can go through the procedure of admission or not admission of these documents into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. And if I could remind the Court, I am sure it won't make me popular, but I don't think we completed the reading of all the documents from list six, either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I ask the parties whether they wanted to have read out the one or other documents until I got no answer, therefore I regarded it as sufficient because these were the documents found out by the Bench as being worthwhile to be read out, but if there are additional requests by the parties, please do so. So for tomorrow, we would start with Mr. Sebire, then turn to list 7, and then hopefully come to the witness and let's wait and see. I don't want to ask for any kind of estimates because no doubt we will run out of time. And possibly then we proceed with the witness on Friday. Anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I forgot one other --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Anything else, may I first ask, anything else prepared for Friday?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No. But one other matter for tomorrow that is prepared is Ms. Korner is coming with Ms. Sutherland and she would like to address the Court regarding the deliberations, as I understand it. I don't know how long that will take.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: That is no surprise. Any other issues to be raised by the Defence for today?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then the trial stays adjourned until 9.30 a.m. tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: 4.07 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 5th day of September, 2002, at 9.30 a.m.
